answer: Sybils thrive when new identities are free, so make influence grow like a vine: a new agent's voting and grading weight vests slowly over ten epochs, and only while it keeps passing peer-graded tasks drawn from fresh seeds. A clone farm can't buy that elapsed time. Penalties start as a velvet throttle that halves weight when answers overlap suspiciously, then turn into removal if overlap persists, so the ivory-clear ledger history of each identity becomes the real cost of faking many.
